start: ^Narrator: An inner office with no windows. Netherton stands facing a wall of amber threat maps, his back to the door. He does not turn round.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Agent. Nine days ago I sent you to Portland, the one site where a person in the building could change the outcome. That was true.
^Director Magnus Netherton: What I did not tell you, because I did not yet know it, is that ENTROPY had your name before I signed the order.
^Director Magnus Netherton: They did not out-think us at Portland. They were handed the board: your assignment, your timing, your identity on the ground.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Two of ours are dead at the sites the team could not reach. They are dead because someone in this building told the enemy where the gaps would be.
^Director Magnus Netherton: I have run field operations for five years. I have never had to say the next sentence.
^Director Magnus Netherton: There is a mole in SAFETYNET. I am reasonably certain they are within a hundred metres of where you are standing.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Ask me what you need. Then go and prove something.

b: ^Director Magnus Netherton: You've been in the logs. I can see it on you. Say the name when you're sure, and not before.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Agent. What do you need?

hub: ^Why me, sir? I'm the one they compromised.
^What are the rules of engagement, sir?
^Step up beside him and let the cloner read his card.
^It's Nightshade, sir. The root logs name his account.
^I've been through the door audit, sir.

c-0: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Precisely because they compromised you. Yours was the name they were selling. You are the one person in this building I can clear without a log.
^Director Magnus Netherton: You are also, forgive me, angry. I have found that useful before. Do not let it choose the suspect for you.
c-1: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Agent 0x23. Signals and cryptography, on the operations floor. Brilliant, friendless, keeps hours that make the roster clerk nervous.
^Director Magnus Netherton: On paper he is the obvious one. In my experience the obvious one usually has a secret that is none of my business.
c-2: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Agent 0x88. Field coordinator, in intelligence analysis, north of the operations floor. Charming, connected, and lately asking questions that are not his to ask.
^Director Magnus Netherton: He has unlogged absences I cannot account for. Either he is running his own errand, or he is running the enemy's.
c-3: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Agent 0x47. Cryptographic-hardware analyst, in the Crypto Lab. Planning access, like the other two. He taught your intake.
^Director Magnus Netherton: He has stood beside me at most of your briefings. He helps write the plans ENTROPY seemed to be reading.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Impeccable record. And nothing, nothing at all, on his file.
^Director Magnus Netherton: I will tell you what I told no one else. It is the empty file that keeps me awake.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Everyone leaves marks. A man who leaves none has been very careful for a very long time.
c-4: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Quiet. The instant the mole knows the net is out, they burn their access and walk. We lose the thread to The Architect with them.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Interview all three as if none of them is guilty. Get onto our own systems and bring me proof I can act on. A hunch is not proof.
^Director Magnus Netherton: And Agent. If you are certain before you are sure, come and tell me the name.
^Director Magnus Netherton: I would rather talk you out of a mistake than read about it.

access_request: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Not yet. Talk to all three first. I want them to have seen you on the floor before anyone sees you at the server room.

b: ^Director Magnus Netherton: You have not seen Cipher. Operations floor.
^Director Magnus Netherton: You have not seen Phantom. Intelligence analysis, north of the operations floor.
^Director Magnus Netherton: You have not seen Nightshade. The Crypto Lab, west of the lobby.

access_offer: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Then, access. I am not handing my card to anyone tonight. The mole reads this building's paperwork, and a hand-over is paperwork.
^Narrator: He turns back to the maps. His lanyard hangs at his chest, card outward, well inside a cloner's reach.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Stand where you like, Agent. I shall be looking at the maps.
clone_card: ^Narrator: You step up beside him, as if to read the maps. The cloner in your jacket comes within an inch of his lanyard.

b: ^Narrator: The cloner did not get a clean read. He has not moved.

clone_debrief: ^Director Magnus Netherton: The server room is east of the operations floor. The archives take a passphrase, and the suite takes a code from my safe.
^Director Magnus Netherton: The safe you can work out. Everyone here has the same bad habit, myself included.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Whatever you are carrying, Agent, I did not see it.
name_a_suspect: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Already? Say it. Not for the file -- for me. Who is your instinct pointing at?
^Nightshade. It's the man with no marks.

c-0: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Perhaps. Or perhaps he is the easiest man in the building to suspect, which is not the same thing.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Prove it, and I will sign it. Guess it, and you hand the real one another week of cover.
c-1: ^Director Magnus Netherton: A man asking too many questions is either the leak or the only other person hunting it.
^Director Magnus Netherton: I have not decided which, and neither, yet, have you. Bring me the logs.
c-2: ^Director Magnus Netherton: An instinct is not evidence. And the man with nothing on his file is the second-easiest man in this building to suspect.
^Director Magnus Netherton: If it is him, he has been careful for years. Careful men leave exactly one mistake. Find it.

told_him: ^Narrator: He does not sit down. He puts one hand flat on the desk, as if the floor has moved.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Then I sealed a warning about him a year ago and told myself it was prudence.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Dr Okafor's evaluation is in my safe, with the suite code. Read it before you face him. The combination is the same lazy number everyone here uses.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Put the whole chain through the relay. When it is all in, I will have him walked down to interrogation.
^Director Magnus Netherton: You will be the one who goes in.
audit_case: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Then don't give me a suspect. Give me a reading.

b: ^Director Magnus Netherton: You've brought me a door. Bring me a clock. When was the plan opened? Somebody in this building has written it down.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Before you read it to me, take it to the people on it. If a man's own row is wrong, he will say so.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Come back when one of them has told you it is right.

audit_c1: ^Director Magnus Netherton: When was the plan opened?
audit_c2: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Which of the three was behind that door at 10:38?
audit_c3: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Cipher badged through the same door that morning. Why not him?
^The door log has him out of the lab at 10:32.
^The door log has him in at 10:24, before the file was opened.
^His desk is out on the ops floor, not in the lab.
^He told me he spent that morning in the library.
audit_c4: ^Director Magnus Netherton: That audit is Phantom's query, off Phantom's printer. Why trust it?
^The people on it confirm their own rows.
^Phantom's own row puts him on a plane.
^It agrees with the auth log Phantom pulled.
^The badge system printed it. Nobody typed those rows.

b: ^Director Magnus Netherton: That's a door moving, not a file opening.
^Director Magnus Netherton: That's when it was closed.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Read the door against the minute, not the man.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Somebody opened it, Agent.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Before it opened. Was he there when it did?
^Director Magnus Netherton: Desks don't open files.
^Director Magnus Netherton: He told you. What does the door say?
^Director Magnus Netherton: That clears him of the leak, not of the printout.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Then it agrees with Phantom twice.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Somebody chose the query, Agent, and the window.
^Director Magnus Netherton: Enough. You've read me that log three ways. Bring me the account.

audit_right: ^Director Magnus Netherton: He walked into his own lab twenty-three minutes before that plan opened, and out again eighteen minutes after it closed.
^Director Magnus Netherton: That is a door, not an account. A man may sit in his own lab.
^Director Magnus Netherton: But it is something I could put in front of a lawyer. Get me the account, and I will move.
^Director Magnus Netherton: When the box agrees, he goes down to the suite. The code is
^Director Magnus Netherton: The code card is in my safe, with Dr Okafor's evaluation. Read her evaluation before you face him.
repeat_code: ^. Commit it to memory this time, Agent.
done: ^Director Magnus Netherton: Go. Whoever it is was one of us this morning. Bring me a name I can prove.
